# Regression: two distinct, spec-valid DSDL types in one namespace that differ only in case/underscore
# style (`FooBar.1.0` and `Foo_bar.1.0`) both snake_case to the same generated file/module stem
# (`foo_bar_1_0`) in the Go/Rust/TypeScript/Python backends, so one output file silently overwrote the
# other and an entire type was lost. The frontend now rejects the pair up front (the case-insensitive
# filesystem check does not catch underscore-only differences). Types whose snake_case stems actually
# differ (`foobar` vs `foo_bar`) must still be accepted. See the type-filename-collision finding.

# RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t/dsdl/ns

# Colliding pair -> hard error (no silent type loss).
# RUN: printf 'uint8 a\n@sealed\n' > %t/dsdl/ns/FooBar.1.0.dsdl
# RUN: printf 'uint16 b\n@sealed\n' > %t/dsdl/ns/Foo_bar.1.0.dsdl
# `ast` emits nothing, so it checks every backend and names the ones affected.
# RUN: not %dsdlc --target-language ast %t/dsdl 2>&1 | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=COLLIDE
# COLLIDE: type name collision in generated output: {{.*}} map to the same output file name for target languages 'rust', 'go', 'ts', 'python'

# Distinct snake stems (foobar vs foo_bar) must NOT be rejected, and both files are generated.
# RUN: rm -rf %t/ok && mkdir -p %t/ok/ns
# RUN: printf 'uint8 a\n@sealed\n' > %t/ok/ns/foobar.1.0.dsdl
# RUN: printf 'uint8 a\n@sealed\n' > %t/ok/ns/foo_bar.1.0.dsdl
# RUN: %dsdlc --target-language go %t/ok --outdir %t/go --go-module ok
# RUN: ls %t/go/ok/ns | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=OK
# OK-DAG: foobar_1_0.go
# OK-DAG: foo_bar_1_0.go
